backbeat: Snare on beats 2 and 4 of a 4/4 bar.
two and four: Beats 2 and 4; usually where the snare or claps go.
one and three: Beats 1 and 3; usually where the kick goes.
four on the floor: Kick on every beat (1, 2, 3, 4), as in house and disco.
downbeat: Beat 1 of the bar; also any main beat as opposed to an offbeat.
on the one: On beat 1, the first beat of the bar.
offbeat, upbeat, the and: The & between beats: the second eighth note of a beat (& of 1, & of 2, ...).
the and of two: The & of 2: halfway between beat 2 and beat 3. Speech recognition may write 'and' as 'end'.
e and a: Sixteenth-note counting is 1 e & a: e is the second sixteenth of a beat, & the third, a the fourth.
trip-let: Triplet counting is 1 trip let: three even pulses per beat.
quarter notes: One hit per beat.
eighth notes, eighths, straight eighths: Two hits per beat: on the beat and the &.
sixteenth notes, sixteenths: Four hits per beat: 1 e & a.
thirty-second notes: Eight hits per beat.
half notes: One hit every two beats: beats 1 and 3 in 4/4.
whole note: One hit per bar, on beat 1.
every other beat: Beats 1 and 3 in 4/4, or 2 and 4 if starting from 2.
half-time: A groove that feels half as fast at the same tempo: snare on beat 3 instead of 2 and 4. As a tempo request ('half time', 'half the speed') it can mean halving the BPM.
double-time: A groove that feels twice as fast: snare on every & or every beat. As a tempo request it can mean doubling the BPM.
syncopation, syncopated: Hits placed off the main beats, on &s, e's or a's.
anticipation, push: A hit just before a beat, on the & or a of the previous beat.
ghost note: A very quiet snare hit. This player has no dynamics, so ghost notes are ordinary snare hits.
accent: A louder hit. This player has no dynamics.
fill: A one-off drum variation at the end of a phrase. This player loops a single bar, so fills aren't supported.
busy, sparse: Busy means more hits; sparse or stripped-down means fewer.
groove, beat, pattern, loop: The repeating drum pattern of one bar.
bar, measure: One cycle of the beats per bar.
kick, bass drum, kick drum: The kick lane.

items.key: snare, rimshot, cross-stick, side stick, clap
items.text: snare, rimshot, cross-stick, side stick, clap: The snare lane; claps and rimshots also go here.

items.key: hi-hat, hat, hats, closed hat, open hat, ride, cymbal, shaker
items.text: hi-hat, hat, hats, closed hat, open hat, ride, cymbal, shaker: The hat lane; ride and other timekeeping cymbals go here.
tom, toms, crash, cowbell, percussion: Not available; the player only has kick, snare and hat.
swing, swung, shuffle: Delaying every second subdivision for a lilting, triplet-like feel. Shuffle is heavy swing.
straight: No swing; evenly spaced subdivisions.
triplet feel, 12/8 feel: Three subdivisions per beat.
common time, 4/4: Four beats per bar.
3/4, waltz: Three beats per bar, accent on 1.
6/8: Two dotted-quarter pulses per bar with three subdivisions each: 2 beats, 3 subdivisions.
12/8: Four dotted-quarter pulses with three subdivisions each: 4 beats, 3 subdivisions.
5/4, 7/4: Five or seven beats per bar.
7/8: Seven eighth notes per bar, usually counted as 7 beats.
cut time, 2/2: Two half-note beats per bar: 2 beats, 2 subdivisions.
count-in, count off: Counting 'one, two, three, four' before the music starts, which sets the tempo.
BPM, tempo: Beats per minute; this player supports 20 to 320.
click, metronome: Regular mode: a plain metronome without the drum grid, on either sound set.

items.key: drum loop, drum machine, custom drum pattern
items.text: drum loop, drum machine, custom drum pattern: Custom drum mode: the kick, snare and hat grid plays.
drums, drum kit, drum sounds: Usually the drum kit sound set, which plays in either mode; beeps are the other set. Not custom drum mode by itself.
tresillo: 3+3+2 pattern: hits on 1, & of 2 and 4 in 4/4 (positions 0, 1.5, 3).
clave: Son clave over two bars; in one bar of 4/4 the 3-side is 1, & of 2, 4.
one drop: Reggae: kick and snare together on beat 3 only, nothing on 1.
skank: Offbeat chops on every &.
boom bap: Hip-hop: kick on 1 (and often the & of 2 or 3), snare on 2 and 4.
train beat: Country: steady snare eighths or sixteenths with kick on 1 and 3.
double the hats: Twice as many hat hits, e.g. eighths become sixteenths.

items.text: move it back, move it forward: Back means earlier in the bar, forward means later.
